newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News Corp U.S. TV profits fall in Q1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News Corp U.S. TV profits fall in Q1.

text.p: Global media group The News Corp Ltd said on Tuesday that profits from its U.S. television stations and its Fox Broadcasting television network fell in the three months to September 30.
Revenues from television fell to A$660 million from A$691 million in the same quarter a year earlier, dragging down operating income to A$67 million from A$111 million.

"At the U.S. television station group, results were impacted by lower earnings at two of its major market stations, New York and Washington D.C., as well as the absence in the quarter of earnings from the company's Atlanta station which was sold in the second quarter last fiscal year," News said.

"At Fox Broadcasting, the poor coverage of several of its new shows and losses at Fox Sports associated with its coverage of the regular season games of Major League Baseball and initially lower ratings for the NFL reduced profits," it said.
Earlier, News Corp reported a group net profit of A$283 million for the quarter ended September 30, down from A$308 million a year earlier.
Net profit before abnormals was A$285 million from A$284 million a year earlier, but was well down on analysts' expectations of A$320 million to A$330 million.

News said, however that, subsequent to the quarter end, U.S. television ratings had improved, led by the broadcast of the World Series, the record setting premiere of Millenium and the strong Sunday debut of the X Files.
Fox had been the number one network in the week ended October 27, its first winning week ever and the first time a network had won the entire week since the 1994 Olympics.
